question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tools.confirmation gate, or keep tool approval enforcement in exec/plugin/action-specific primitives?
rationale: The evidence shows a real safety gap, but the permanent shape changes core authorization semantics and config surface, so automation should not choose the policy boundary.

options.title: Sponsor core gate
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and design a backward-compatible core confirmation policy that composes with existing approvals.

options.title: Narrow to plugin/API seams
options.body: Route the work to missing plugin or trusted-policy APIs if maintainers want core to stay policy-neutral.

options.title: Decline central gate
options.body: Close this only if maintainers explicitly accept keeping authorization at per-tool/plugin/operator layers.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core gate
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and design a backward-compatible core confirmation policy that composes with existing approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on before_tool_call and hook context makes this the closest available routing owner for the technical policy boundary.
